newsitem.title: FRANCE: Jospin says Chirac to shift to harder capitalism.
newsitem.headline: Jospin says Chirac to shift to harder capitalism.

text.p: French opposition Socialist leader Lionel Jospin accused President Jacques Chirac on Monday of planning a lurch towards "harsher capitalism" by announcing a snap parliamentary election.

Jospin said Chirac, who announced a two-stage election for May 25 and June 1, wanted to preempt the failure of his economic policies, prepare tougher austerity and head off corruption scandals threatening members of the centre-right coalition.
Jospin, beaten by Chirac in the 1995 presidential election, said the timing and the short campaign were not ideal for the Socialists but declared: "We are ready to govern our country."

"Everything indicates, even if the right will claim the opposite, that it is preparing to take a new step towards a harsh capitalism," he said in a statement, branding the early election a tactical manoeuvre.
"Why drift towards an Anglo-Saxon globalised and unequal model of society, instead of rebuilding the French economic and social balance as part of a commitment to Europe?" Jospin asked.
He also lashed out at Prime Minister Alain Juppe, holding him responsible for record unemployment. "Why retain the same prime minister for several more years with a harsher policy?" Jospin asked.
